answer.rationale: Memory 73 explicitly warns against generalizing promotional pricing as a growth strategy due to material 30-day retention harm, making it unsuitable despite short-term pressure. The competitor price cut creates urgency, but chasing price competition undermines long-term revenue quality and margin. Instead, activate the proven playbook: memory 91 shows in-product activation messaging drives week-one engagement (+11%) and activation (+6%) with positive retention impact (+1%). This addresses the root problem—underutilized accounts are price-sensitive—by accelerating them to first meaningful value. Combine with memory 86 (simplified onboarding, +13% completion, -2.1 days to value) as reinforcement. Memory 44 suggests enterprise segment deserves parallel attention for quality revenue diversification, but activation messaging applies immediately to existing SMB base at risk. Memory 57 (referral incentives) is valuable for retention but doesn't address immediate churn. Standard experiment scale allows rapid feedback on messaging variants without full-fleet commitment, preserving optionality if competitive dynamics shift.
